name: Sri Lanka
aliases: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

language.script_notes: Sinhala script (rounded, loop-heavy letters) is unique to Sri Lanka and the single most definitive tell. Tamil script also appears and is shared with Tamil Nadu in India, so Tamil alone is ambiguous — but the mix of Sinhala and Tamil on bilingual signs, often far from Tamil-majority areas, points to Sri Lanka. English appears widely as a third language on signage.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Small white and black stone bollards; some yellow-and-black striped variants documented.
road_furniture.line_paint: Yellow outside/white inside or white outside/white inside lines.
road_furniture.curb_style: Black-and-white painted curb blocks appear near canals and at intersections — a distinctive Sri Lanka tell, with bollards showing up frequently alongside.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Two common utility-pole types: one with see-through 'holey' openings in the lower half of the pole, and one with small holes only near the top. Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CEYPETCO), Lanka IOC and Laugfs are common fuel-station brands.

architecture.roof_style: Red clay tile pitched roofs are the default on houses and shophouses; Portuguese-style pitched roofs with balconies visible in colonial-era coastal areas.
architecture.roof_material: Red clay tile very common nationwide; corrugated metal on simpler buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Concrete-block and stucco houses in whitewashed or pastel tones; Buddhist temples (viharas) with white dagobas (bell-shaped stupas) are a defining feature — Sri Lanka's stupas are among the largest brick structures in the world; Dutch colonial forts (Galle) and British hill-station architecture in the central highlands.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White and pastel tones on houses and temples; brightly painted shopfronts and Hindu kovil temples in Tamil areas.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: White dome-shaped dagobas (stupas) topped with a conical spire; Buddhist viharas; brightly coloured Hindu kovil temples with tiered gopuram-style towers in Tamil regions; Dutch-era Galle Fort; colonial-era tea-estate bungalows in the hill country.

nature.vegetation: Coconut palms line the coastal lowlands; tea plantations blanket the central highlands (Nuwara Eliya, Kandy region); rice paddies fill the wet-zone lowlands; dry-zone scrub in the north and east.
nature.terrain: A tropical island with a flat coastal belt, a mountainous central highland region with tea-covered hills and waterfalls, and a drier northern/eastern plain; ancient man-made irrigation reservoirs ('tanks') dot the dry zone.
nature.climate_signature: Hot and humid tropical climate with two monsoons — lush green in the wet southwest, drier in the north and east.

vehicles.plate_color: Rear plates are yellow with black text while front plates are white — one of the few countries with this yellow-rear/white-front split.
vehicles.plate_format: Province code letters + digits (e.g. 'CAB-1234'), historically with Sinhala letters in older formats.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Three-wheeler tuk-tuks (typically Bajaj, often painted in bright colours) are extremely common; buses are colourful and heavily decorated; Suzuki kei-style small cars and vans widespread.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3/4 official coverage; the car uses a lower camera mount that produces a distinctive larger visible blur at the bottom of the frame, a look shared with only a few countries (Japan, Switzerland, parts of India).
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring plus the distinctive large low-mounted car blur.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage across most of the island, including the tea-covered central highlands and coastal belt.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Tamil script in the north of Sri Lanka, similar tropical coastal palm vegetation and tuk-tuk culture, both drive on the left
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Sinhala script is unique to Sri Lanka and settles it instantly; Sri Lanka's yellow-rear/white-front plates, black-and-white curb blocks and small stone bollards also differ from India's road furniture and plate formats.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Nearby South Asian island nation with similar tropical coastal vegetation
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Maldives uses Dhivehi (Thaana) script and is composed of tiny low-lying coral islands with almost no roads by comparison; Sri Lanka's larger island geography and road network are very different.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Theravada Buddhist temples with white stupas, similar tropical vegetation and tuk-tuk transport, both drive on the left
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Sinhala script and dagobas (bell-shaped stupas) vs. Thai script and ornate multi-tiered Thai wat roofs; Sri Lanka's yellow rear plates are a distinctive tell absent in Thailand.
